column1: # MEASURED exon inclusion, from published assays. NOT model output, and not a
# correction applied to model output: a separate quantity, displayed as such.
# This file exists because a handful of clinically important exons sit in
# duplicated sequence, where short-read PSI is a blend of two genes and no model
# trained on that label can be right (see untrusted.py). For those, a number
# someone actually measured beats both the blend and a prediction.
# KEYED ON THE EXON START, not on a start-end pair. The start is exact and comes
# from the event table; carrying an end as well would mean carrying an exon
# length too, and a length that is wrong by a base silently stops the row
# matching. A row matches an annotated exon when its start falls inside it.
# psi is the central published figure and psi_lo/psi_hi the spread across
# assays, because this is not a constant: it varies with cell type, SMN2 copy
# number and whether the measurement is of an endogenous gene or a reporter.
# Showing a bare 0.10 would trade one false precision for another.
# Add a row only with a citation that a reader can check. An uncited row is
# worse than no row, because it looks like evidence.
